## [issue:surrealdb/surrealdb#7472] (issue) Transaction::commit() on local engines discards QueryError::TransactionConflict, so conflict-retry never fires#7472
https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/issues/7472
# Transaction::commit() on local engines discards QueryError::TransactionConflict, so conflict-retry never fires#7472
## Description
### What component does this affect?
Rust SDK

### Describe the bug
**The asymmetry:** the _query_ path in the same file does not flatten. `Command::Query` / the 3.3 `query` arm return `execute_with_transaction`'s results directly, so a conflict raised **while a statement executes** keeps its kind. Only `commit` (and `rollback`, harmless — nothing classifies a rollback failure) flattens.

Note this is the path most embedded application code and most examples use.

### Steps to reproduce

### SurrealDB version
Also verified present in **3.3.0-beta.1**, where the code moved to the new `surrealdb-engine-local` crate — the surrounding logic there was reworked (abandoned-transaction handling, claim-by-removal), but the error flattening is unchanged.

tsondru

## Harness

## Distinct errors observed
| path | `query_details()` | n | `to_string()` |
|-|-|-|-|
| `tx.commit()`, Mem | **`None`** | 952 | `Transaction conflict: Write conflict, retry the transaction. This transaction can be retried` |

## Source (unchanged from the original report, re-verified at `3.3.0-beta.1`)
Dhghomon

Hi @tsondru,

This has been fixed so that it returns `QueryError::TransactionConflict` from `commit()` instead of an internal error that carries only the message, so a retry on conflict can match on the error kind.

## [issue:surrealdb/surrealdb#7428] (issue) Expose retryable transaction write-conflict as a public typed error / is_retryable()#7428
https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/issues/7428
# Expose retryable transaction write-conflict as a public typed error / is_retryable()#7428
#7429

Improvement

#7429

## Summary
When two transactions concurrently write the same record on the embedded engine (SurrealKV), the losing transaction fails with a write conflict that is meant to be retried. On the public Rust SDK there is currently no _typed_ / stable way to detect "this failure is a retryable write-conflict" — it can only be recognized by string-matching the error message, which is fragile across releases.

## Observed behaviour (SurrealDB `3.1.5`, surrealkv `0.21.2`)
The conflict is only visible via `Response::take_errors()`, where the COMMIT statement carries:

## Minimal repro (public API only)

Under a multi-threaded runtime this produces many `take_errors()` entries containing the conflict message; there is no non-string way to classify them as retryable.

Actually it looks like that issue was fixed in 3.2.2 [https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.2](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.2), I'm now getting the expected TransactionConflict error details

Hi @jleni,

This is now resolved since 3.2.2 with its own typed error and the ability to retry. This page has more details: [https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/errors#error-details](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/errors#error-details)

## [doc:https://github.com/surrealdb/docs.surrealdb.com/blob/cdf782611d3404fe9acbd039607de2d763f91ff7/src/content/reference/javascript/concepts/executing-queries.mdx] (doc) Executing queries
# Executing queries
## Running raw SurrealQL

## Retrying on write conflict
Under concurrent write load, a query can fail with a read/write conflict when another transaction touched the same data. Chain `.retry()` onto `.query()` or any query builder method to replay the operation automatically with exponential backoff.

Retry is off by default, and only applies to `.collect()` (or awaiting the query directly) - not `.responses()` or `.stream()`. For raw queries with multiple statements, only enable it when the statements are safe to apply more than once, since a retried query re-sends the whole thing.
